Armored Core 6 is an absolute masterpiece of a game. I can say this because I found absolutely nothing to complain about, and anything that there was to complain about would have been so laughably minor that it wouldn't matter. I loved this game so much that I replayed it twice to get all 3 endings, which I highly suggest everyone who plays this game does.

I'm left wanting more Armored Core, as there just isn't anything like this game. It's fast-paced, extremely customizable, and really fun. I ran with a few different builds that I had made, and when talking to my friends we all ran completely different builds that all looked so wildly different from each other.

If you're on the fence, I can assure you that this game is different and it's worth the time you invest into it. Even if this game isn't on sale, it is well worth it's price tag. 

I can't wait to see where this series goes in the future.

Aesthetically, one of the greatest players in NBA Franchise History. The Tim Duncan of video games. This thing is freakin’ hard though, brother. I’m steadily getting through it, but it’s not quite the difficulty I was expecting on the first playthrough (versus NG+) based on how it was marketed, so I can see how dudes could get ticked off by it. You jump from battling Level 1 Pipsqueaks to Shotgun Surgeons on a whim. It’s not the greatest of pacing for many.

You HAVE to beat the boss at face value. No summons, no co-op, no difficulty select. You just signed up for Sekiro 2, playa. If you’re looking to have a laid back time and play mech dress-up, you can’t, and that can suck! I feel like I’m playing like my house is gonna explode if I lose, and while that’s fun sometimes, I definitely expected a difficulty similar to Normal/Hard in Ace Combat 7, or even past Armored Core games like 4a. I was using builds I found satisfying, but had to switch to some cheese tactics if I got stuck, and the encounters were STILL tough.

All in all, I’m very much having a good time, but as someone who doesn’t play souls the most often, I gotta accept that I’m gonna get two piece’d out here. If you’re thinking about getting it, just keep that in mind. This game is not like the others in the series.

I’ll start with this: Armored Core 6 is a phenomenal game. The movement is smooth, the combat is intense, and the customization is deep. FromSoftware really nailed the feeling of piloting a high-speed war machine, dashing across the battlefield, dodging missiles, and unloading an arsenal of weapons in a way that feels incredibly fluid and satisfying. The boss fights are brutal but rewarding, pushing you to fine-tune your build and adapt your tactics constantly.

That said, this isn’t my kind of mech game. I prefer the slower, more tactical, and methodical combat of MechWarrior, where positioning, heat management, and armor distribution matter more than sheer mobility and reflexes. Armored Core 6 is the opposite: it’s fast, aggressive, and demands quick thinking and high-speed execution. If that’s what you’re looking for, this game delivers in spades.

So while it’s not exactly what I personally enjoy in a mech game, I can still wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who loves fast-paced mech action, deep customization, and challenging combat. It’s a fantastic experience, just one that caters to a different style of mech combat than what I typically enjoy.

After refunding the game on release, I really felt like a FromSoftware game, that wasn't my 8th playthrough of Elden Ring. I gave Armored Core another go and actually quite enjoyed the game after I realized how much your loadout actually matters in this game, which equally needs to fit your playstyle. I ended up with dual pistol + melee finisher, mostly light bot and realized the campaign wasn't that difficult, it was arguably a little easy one-shotting most bosses first try. Mind you, the multiplayer is still played, but at the time of writing this review, only 1500 people are playing it. Expect to be fighting absolute tryhards. Which is my main point of critique on this game. All the things you unlock for multiplayer you unlock in the singleplayer which is a good 30-40 hour grind to unlock everything. if you choose to ignore this, you will realize very quick multiplayer is a whole different balpark.

This reminds me of the days when I played the PS2 with the difficulty, customization, and story on point for this series. I do want more parts in the game and I hope to see this series more in my lifetime.

Fun game. Make big mech. Fight fast intense battles. Game is hard.

Sometimes you'll run into a specific level or boss that requires a redesign, but I was able to go through most of the game with a single build. Lightweight with two pistols and a melee weapon.

My biggest complaint is that there are three total endings. NG, NG+, and NG++. In order to get all three endings you have to play through the entire game three times, but only a few small things change each time: a couple new missions, additional enemies in a few missions, a couple alternate choices. Your second and third playthroughs are a lot faster than your first because you're already familiar with the missions, but it still feels a bit like "Look! The game is replayable and therefore has more value!" without actually adding much value.

I would still recommend though. Very fun.

Everything I try to write on this line, I end up saying it's my favourite part of the game. so I'll just list them off:

Firstly, The customization in this game is so extensive you'll get choice paralysis from all the stuff you can use

Second, The combat mechanics are just the right amount of varied, complex, and intuitive that it never gets old, and at the same time doesn't get confusing.

Third: the GUI is so beautiful, yet so simplistic. reminiscent of those infrared tracking cameras they put on military aircraft. Love it.

Fourth: The Graphics (sorry). when you're not in combat, they're beautiful in the 'breathtaking scenery' kind of way, and when you are in combat, they're beautiful in the 'fireworks show' kind of way.

Fourth.5: The general aesthetic of the game is the BEST. I'm really into Automation games and Industrial Sci-Fi so this is just the thing for me. if you're into those things, you'll love this too

Fifth: The Plot. no spoilers, but trust me its good

My first Armored Core game. As a fan of ER, souls and sekiro, and as a fan of Mech Warrior games I really loved AC6.
This game is carried by its gameplay no doubt, but I loved the story too. Especially the fragmented and incomplete manner in which it is told, which leaves a lot up to player's interpretation and gives some food for thought.

I don't mind the story being separated between NG, NG+, NG++ - very similar to Nier Automata's story structure. But I don't get why not just make those 3 playthroughs linear. Because you can miss out on some of the decision missions as a result. Which is just unnecessary headache. Or at least it should unlock all the possible missions once players have completed NG++ or reached all the endings.

Update 1/4/2024

patch 1.05 released about 2 weeks ago, introducing a new set of AC parts and 4 new weapons, alongside ranked PVP matchmaking.

The new added AC parts and weapons are lots of fun to use, but ranked pvp has quite a few issues. players abusing poor internet connections take advantage of the near instantaneous travel time of laser weapons to almost never miss shots. these laser builds, combined with other setups designed to exploit poor server connections as well as the missile boat "rat" setups make PVP a sweaty and enjoyment deprived space. My point still stands that Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon is my personal GOTY, but a more expansive multiplayer was definitely something people were looking forward to. as it currently stands, I still very much enjoy Armored Core VI but the multiplayer aspects of the game leave much to be desired.
